albedo.assumption: albedo 0.04 is an assumption adopted by the authors to convert H_V into a size; no measurement of the albedo exists
albedo.source: literature: Meech et al. 2017, Nature 552, 378, Methods, 'Shape and size': p = 0.04 adopted (backend/assets/literature.toml). Assumed, not measured

band_depth_3um.source: not available: no source in the pipeline yet (no band-depth rule in the specs)

diameter_km.assumption: geometric albedo 0.04 is assumed, not measured (Meech et al. adopt it); the size follows from H_V = 22.4 and that albedo
diameter_km.source: literature: Meech et al. 2017, Nature 552, 378, Methods, 'Shape and size': mean radius 102 +/- 4 m at p = 0.04 (backend/assets/literature.toml). Diameter = 2 x 102 m. The paper calls linear dimensions from the magnitudes alone meaningless because a/c is unconstrained; the +/- is from the magnitudes only

gaia_rgb.formula: Gaia DR3 colours to RGB (not computed)
gaia_rgb.source: not available: the Gaia adapter is not built (A3.2)

lightcurve_amp_mag.source: literature: Meech et al. 2017, Nature 552, 378, Methods, 'Shape and size': light-curve range 2.5 mag (g = 22.15 brightest, 24.65 faintest) (backend/assets/literature.toml). Axis ratio 10:1 or more; c is unconstrained, so cigar versus disc is open. The spin is tumbling (period 7.34 +/- 0.06 h, double-peaked assumption); not drawn

phase_angle_deg.source: JPL Horizons quantity 24 (Sun-Target-Observer), observer SPHEREx 500@-163182, at 2026-11-14T00:00:00.000Z

rot_period_h.source: JPL SBDB rot_per (LCDB (Rev. 2023-October); Warner et al., 2009)

slope_075_25.source: not available: the only published slope (23 +/- 3 %/100 nm, Meech et al. 2017) is optical (g to Y, about 0.5 to 1.0 um), while this field covers 0.75 to 2.5 um and its unit is not settled (docs say %/um, code reads %/100 nm); no 0.75 to 2.5 um slope is published

spectral_class.source: not available: no catalogue class; spectrum matching is not built (A4.3)

spherex_rgb.source: not available: no SPHEREx spectrum for this object

sun_vector.formula: -r/|r|, r = heliocentric ICRF position from JPL Horizons VECTORS (CENTER 500@10) at 2026-11-14T00:00:00.000Z; frame ICRF (equatorial J2000), direction target to Sun

render_params.alt_text: 'Oumuamua (A/2017 U1), Asteroid, 0.204 km across (model dependent), no visible colour basis, viewed at 0.755 degrees. Surface relief: illustrative.

assumed.c_axis: c is not constrained by a light curve; c = b draws a cigar, and a disc fits the same data

layers.description: Assumption: a/b = 10^(0.4 * A), c = b, from the light-curve amplitude (R6.2).

Procedural height field from the seed: a rubble pile of rock and shattered rock; lumps from rock strength against gravity (h/R = 0.30), craters N(>D) ~ D^-2, boulders by structure. Rough and rocky is the default: only a shape model, radar roughness or thermal inertia could make it smoother, and the card has none. The density is a generic value (1500 kg/m3), an assumption (R6.2, R6.3, D-36).
Surface pushed in and out by the height map, over a range of 1 of the radius (R6.2, R7.2, D-36).
